{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Extend the existing Spring XD container and module configuration model rather than introducing a separate configuration subsystem.",
    "Represent external-service bindings and environment variables as container-level configuration that can be supplied through Docker environment settings and generated service metadata.",
    "Use a provider-neutral service-discovery abstraction with an initial implementation compatible with the existing deployment conventions; avoid hard-coding application logic to a single discovery product.",
    "Implement CI image creation with reproducible Docker builds, parameterized build arguments, automated tests, and publication to a configurable image registry.",
    "Document Mesos and Marathon deployment as a recommended operational configuration, including scheduler resources, networking, service discovery, persistence, scaling, and failure recovery.",
    "Evaluate Spring Boot dependency upgrades through a controlled dependency change, compilation, unit tests, integration tests, and regression comparison before accepting the upgrade.",
    "Implement RDBMS-to-HDFS partitioning using the existing batch partitioning abstractions, with configurable partition keys, ranges, and worker concurrency.",
    "Implement the HDFS source module using the existing module/source contracts and Hadoop-compatible filesystem APIs, with configurable paths, formats, file matching, and serialization.",
    "Expose commit interval as a configuration property in servers.yml with the existing default preserved and apply it consistently to all out-of-the-box partition-capable jobs.",
    "Use automated unit, integration, configuration, and Docker smoke tests, supplemented by focused manual verification for Mesos/Marathon documentation and deployment scenarios."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment is implemented in an existing Spring XD codebase with established build, module, container, configuration, and test conventions.",
    "The existing project can build with Java 17 or has an available compatible build profile; migration of the entire legacy codebase to Java 17 is out of scope.",
    "Existing Docker container support, module packaging, and deployment descriptors can be extended rather than developed from scratch.",
    "A specific service-discovery product is not mandated; the implementation will support a documented generic contract and the discovery mechanism already used by the target deployment environment.",
    "External services such as RabbitMQ, Redis, Zookeeper, Hadoop, and MongoDB are not implemented; only container configuration, binding, and discovery integration are included.",
    "The CI environment and Docker engine are available, and credentials for an image registry are supplied by the consuming organization.",
    "The CI work includes pipeline configuration and image build/test scripts but not administration of the CI platform or production registry.",
    "The RDBMS partitioning feature targets existing JDBC-based ingest jobs and uses an existing Spring Batch-style partitioning model.",
    "The HDFS source supports the Hadoop client version already used by the project and common text or binary input handling; specialized formats such as Avro, Parquet, and ORC are excluded unless already supported.",
    "The commit-interval setting is a numeric property with validation and a backward-compatible default, and all affected out-of-the-box jobs share a modifiable configuration path.",
    "The Mesos/Marathon deliverable is an operational recommendation document with example configuration, not a production cluster installation or managed service.",
    "One developer performs implementation, testing, documentation, dependency evaluation, and integration work; estimates include normal code review preparation and rework but exclude waiting time for external approvals or infrastructure."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Codebase reconnaissance and increment planning",
      "activity_description": "Inspect existing container, module, deployment, batch, HDFS, configuration, CI, and test structures; identify extension points and produce an implementation plan and acceptance checklist for U1-U8.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Cross-cutting design and configuration model",
      "activity_description": "Define configuration schemas, defaults, validation, compatibility behavior, service-binding metadata, discovery interfaces, and integration boundaries shared by the individual features.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Docker external-service configuration and bindings",
      "activity_description": "Add support for configuring Docker XD containers with external-service linking or binding attributes and environment variables, including examples and configuration validation for services such as RabbitMQ, Redis, Zookeeper, Hadoop, and MongoDB.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Docker service-discovery integration",
      "activity_description": "Implement configurable service-discovery registration and lookup behavior for XD containers, map discovered endpoints into container configuration, handle startup and missing-service cases, and add provider-neutral examples.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "CI Docker image build and deployment artifacts",
      "activity_description": "Create or update Dockerfiles, build scripts, CI pipeline stages, image tagging and parameterization, automated image smoke tests, and registry publication configuration for building deployable XD images.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Mesos and Marathon deployment recommendations",
      "activity_description": "Research the target XD runtime requirements and produce deployment documentation covering Marathon application definitions, resource sizing, networking, service discovery, persistence, scaling, upgrades, health checks, and failure recovery.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Spring Boot dependency upgrade evaluation",
      "activity_description": "Create an isolated dependency-upgrade change, resolve compatibility and transitive dependency issues, run compilation and regression suites, compare behavior with the baseline, and document side effects, risks, and recommendation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "RDBMS-to-HDFS data partitioning strategy",
      "activity_description": "Implement configurable partition strategy support for JDBC/RDBMS ingest jobs, including partition-key or range selection, worker execution settings, validation, partition metadata propagation, and representative partitioned-ingest tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "HDFS source module",
      "activity_description": "Implement and package an HDFS source module using the existing source/module contracts, including filesystem configuration, path and file matching, input handling, error behavior, lifecycle management, documentation, and unit/integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Configurable commit interval for partition-capable jobs",
      "activity_description": "Add the commit-interval property to servers.yml and the relevant job configuration path, preserve the default, validate values, apply it to all applicable out-of-the-box partitioned jobs, and add configuration regression tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Integration, regression, and deployment verification",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and test suite, add cross-feature integration coverage for Docker configuration, discovery, image execution, partitioned ingest, HDFS input, and commit interval behavior, and fix defects found during verification.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Final documentation, packaging, and delivery",
      "activity_description": "Finalize user and operator documentation, configuration examples, release notes, upgrade findings, test evidence, packaging metadata, and implementation handoff materials.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 504
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Extend the existing Spring XD container and module configuration model rather than introducing a separate configuration subsystem.
Represent external-service bindings and environment variables as container-level configuration that can be supplied through Docker environment settings and generated service metadata.

Use a provider-neutral service-discovery abstraction with an initial implementation compatible with the existing deployment conventions; avoid hard-coding application logic to a single discovery product.
Implement CI image creation with reproducible Docker builds, parameterized build arguments, automated tests, and publication to a configurable image registry.
Document Mesos and Marathon deployment as a recommended operational configuration, including scheduler resources, networking, service discovery, persistence, scaling, and failure recovery.
Evaluate Spring Boot dependency upgrades through a controlled dependency change, compilation, unit tests, integration tests, and regression comparison before accepting the upgrade.
Implement RDBMS-to-HDFS partitioning using the existing batch partitioning abstractions, with configurable partition keys, ranges, and worker concurrency.
Implement the HDFS source module using the existing module/source contracts and Hadoop-compatible filesystem APIs, with configurable paths, formats, file matching, and serialization.
Expose commit interval as a configuration property in servers.yml with the existing default preserved and apply it consistently to all out-of-the-box partition-capable jobs.
Use automated unit, integration, configuration, and Docker smoke tests, supplemented by focused manual verification for Mesos/Marathon documentation and deployment scenarios.
assumptions: The increment is implemented in an existing Spring XD codebase with established build, module, container, configuration, and test conventions.
The existing project can build with Java 17 or has an available compatible build profile; migration of the entire legacy codebase to Java 17 is out of scope.
Existing Docker container support, module packaging, and deployment descriptors can be extended rather than developed from scratch.
A specific service-discovery product is not mandated; the implementation will support a documented generic contract and the discovery mechanism already used by the target deployment environment.
External services such as RabbitMQ, Redis, Zookeeper, Hadoop, and MongoDB are not implemented; only container configuration, binding, and discovery integration are included.
The CI environment and Docker engine are available, and credentials for an image registry are supplied by the consuming organization.
The CI work includes pipeline configuration and image build/test scripts but not administration of the CI platform or production registry.
The RDBMS partitioning feature targets existing JDBC-based ingest jobs and uses an existing Spring Batch-style partitioning model.

The HDFS source supports the Hadoop client version already used by the project and common text or binary input handling; specialized formats such as Avro, Parquet, and ORC are excluded unless already supported.
The commit-interval setting is a numeric property with validation and a backward-compatible default, and all affected out-of-the-box jobs share a modifiable configuration path.
The Mesos/Marathon deliverable is an operational recommendation document with example configuration, not a production cluster installation or managed service.

One developer performs implementation, testing, documentation, dependency evaluation, and integration work; estimates include normal code review preparation and rework but exclude waiting time for external approvals or infrastructure.

Define configuration schemas, defaults, validation, compatibility behavior, service-binding metadata, discovery interfaces, and integration boundaries shared by the individual features.

Add support for configuring Docker XD containers with external-service linking or binding attributes and environment variables, including examples and configuration validation for services such as RabbitMQ, Redis, Zookeeper, Hadoop, and MongoDB.

Implement configurable service-discovery registration and lookup behavior for XD containers, map discovered endpoints into container configuration, handle startup and missing-service cases, and add provider-neutral examples.

activities.activity_description: Create or update Dockerfiles, build scripts, CI pipeline stages, image tagging and parameterization, automated image smoke tests, and registry publication configuration for building deployable XD images.

Research the target XD runtime requirements and produce deployment documentation covering Marathon application definitions, resource sizing, networking, service discovery, persistence, scaling, upgrades, health checks, and failure recovery.

Create an isolated dependency-upgrade change, resolve compatibility and transitive dependency issues, run compilation and regression suites, compare behavior with the baseline, and document side effects, risks, and recommendation.

Implement configurable partition strategy support for JDBC/RDBMS ingest jobs, including partition-key or range selection, worker execution settings, validation, partition metadata propagation, and representative partitioned-ingest tests.

Implement and package an HDFS source module using the existing source/module contracts, including filesystem configuration, path and file matching, input handling, error behavior, lifecycle management, documentation, and unit/integration tests.
